name: mor-kishib
description: Kišib: the one place where a chain key is used, from paper, and then forgotten (F335). Rotate an identity from its chain key's words, keeping every line; rotate a collective from its members' paper shares (F337); escape a contested position with both keys; declare a succession and confirm it. It holds nothing between uses. On the Mac and Linux, a program and its page; on the web (kishib.dubsar.org), the same page, for testing only. Test identities only, until MOR is frozen.
